key_insight: A two-stage AI system can infer transcriptome patterns from breast cancer biopsy histology and use them to predict response to neoadjuvant therapy more accurately than pathology-only approaches.
clinical_relevance: This could help identify which breast cancer patients are more likely to achieve pathological complete response, supporting treatment personalization when labeled data are limited.
method: Stage 1: learn transcriptome-associated features from histopathology using 8,742 patients across 32 cancer types.
Stage 2: combine inferred expression with clinical variables to predict pCR in breast cancer cohorts.
Validate against pathologist review, spatial gene-expression agreement, and ablation comparisons.
evidence_signal: Trained on 1,080 patients from five cohorts and evaluated in 1,412 patients across nine cohorts, the model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0.79 (95% CI, 0.73-0.85).
watch_item: The approach still needs careful external validation and workflow testing before routine use, especially because performance may vary across institutions, scanners, and biopsy quality.
paper_title: Transcriptome-informed multi-modal AI for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response from breast cancer biopsies
